title: Ten of the fourteen undated impossibility rows probed: nine hold, return.devices does not reproduce
set: empty set, four tracks, two return tracks carrying Reverb and Delay
question: Fourteen catalog rows told a caller something cannot be done, with an attribution and no measurement. Which of them is true of this Live?
why_it_matters: A false 'cannot' stops a caller from trying, and a catalog row is inherited as fact. The contract hardening spec's acceptance criterion 8.3 asks for every impossibility to be dated and measured, and expects at least one to be wrong.
specimens: Operator and EQ Eight on MIDI track 0
Reverb on return track A, and the same Reverb loaded onto ordinary track 2
Oxi Bass Rack on track 0 for a nested chain device
Simpler on MIDI track 1, made by dropping a sample onto it
one-shot sample dropped onto audio track 3 for an unwarped audio clip
method: lom_set on the path, with its read-back, through the raw tool, which does not consult the row's access list. Values were restored where anything was stored.

results.claim: the parameter object is read-only and lom_set answers not_settable
results.probe: lom_set on the parameter object, then on the same parameter's .value
results.answer: object: not_settable on all five. .value: applied, except the on/off parameter which answered clamped for 0.42 because it holds 0 or 1

results.probe: lom_set with a plausible value, and a track handle for group_track
results.answer: not_settable on all three, with Live naming the attribute in its own message

results.claim: read-only, taken from Ableton's documentation rather than measured
results.probe: read, then lom_set with another path
results.answer: read returned the file on disk; the write answered not_settable. A Simpler with no sample loaded has no .sample at all and answers no_such_path
results.outcome: held, and now measured rather than attributed

results.claim: an unwarped audio clip cannot loop meaningfully, and Live is expected to allow the flag anyway
results.probe: warping set to false on an audio one-shot, then looping set to true
results.answer: applied and changed, reads back true
results.outcome: the expectation is now a reading. The flag is not a guard, so a clip carrying it is no evidence that anything loops

results.claim: a return device's parameters have been seen without display_value where the same device on a normal track provides it, so a dB or Hz target cannot be searched for on a return at all
results.probe: first four parameters of a Reverb in return track A and of the same Reverb loaded onto ordinary track 2
results.answer: the same display_value on both, Predelay reading 2.5 either way, across all four

not_probed.why: the claim is about writing tempo automation, not about writing tempo
the claim is about Live 10 and earlier snapping to a 70-entry palette, which an installation running 12.4.6 cannot show
advice about planning send levels in dB rather than in 0 to 1, which is not an impossibility claim. The check matches it on wording
song.tracks[N].devices[0].chains[0].mixer_device.sends[0] answered index_out_of_range on the rack probed, so no send was there to read

result: The roster falls from fourteen to three. Nine claims hold and now carry a date and a version; one does not reproduce and its row is replaced by the reading.
return.devices carried no date and no version, so what it was true of cannot be established. It is not true of Live 12.4.6 with a Reverb.

The shared sentence behind five of the rows is true and was true for a dull reason: the path names the DeviceParameter object and the number lives one level in, at .value. The rows say so already; what they lacked was the reading.
scope_and_weakness: One device of each kind. return.devices was probed with Reverb alone, so a device whose return instance does drop display_value would not have been seen.
One machine, one Live version, one session, one empty set.
Only the writes were probed. Whether lom_get suffers any asymmetry of its own was not measured.
The three remaining rows are not measured and are not claimed to be right. Two of them cannot be probed on this installation at all.
